site: Greenhouse (Datadog work-authorization list); any list whose rows combine authorization with sponsorship
class: A qualified option ('No, I need sponsorship now') was judged by its first word instead of what it says
symptom: On Datadog the agent chose 'No, I need sponsorship now' -- true for an owner who needs an H-1B transfer -- and safety.legal_answer_conflicts flagged it as 'but you are authorized to work', so the truthfulness declaration was refused.
root_cause: The work-authorization branch of legal_answer_conflicts treated any value starting with 'No' as a denial of authorization, without reading the sponsorship qualifier the same row carries.
why_tests_missed: Its tests used bare Yes/No values; the sponsorship-qualified rows were tested only for choosing (f184), not for checking.
fix: option_match.sponsorship_said(text) is the one reading of what a row says the applicant needs (True / False / None), used by sponsorship_choice and by legal_answer_conflicts: a row that speaks of sponsorship is checked against profile.requires_visa_sponsorship; a bare 'No' is still a denial. _SPONSORED now reads 'need sponsorship' and _UNRESTRICTED 'do/will not need/require sponsorship'.
prevention: Choosing an option and checking the chosen option use the same reading of it; never judge a qualified row by its first word.
